options.reason: An annual count directly shows how the number of motorist deaths changed over time, without implying an exposure-adjusted risk.
options.answer: Motorist fatalities fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but this dataset cannot show whether per-mile fatality risk decreased because it contains no vehicle-miles-traveled data.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual number of motorist deaths declined: it fell from 110 to 81 over the period, though the intervening years fluctuated. The count is a direct measure of fatal outcomes, but it leaves per-mile risk unanswered because the dataset has no miles-driven denominator.

options.reason: Normalizing fatalities by reported crashes provides a severity-per-crash comparison when travel exposure is unavailable.
options.answer: Motorist fatalities per 1,000 reported crashes rose from 0.540 in 2013 to 0.947 in 2025, so this crash-based proxy did not decrease; it cannot establish the per-mile trend without miles driven.
options.interpretation: This framing compares fatality burden relative to the number of reported crashes, and the measure rose from 0.540 to 0.947 fatalities per 1,000 crashes between 2013 and 2025. It is a defensible severity-per-crash proxy, but it leaves the question of per-mile risk unanswered because the dataset does not record vehicle miles traveled.
